cards.title: f-strings fill in values
cards.body: An f-string has `f` before the quote. Anything inside `{}` is replaced with its value.

hi.title: f-strings values bharte hain
hi.body: f-string ke quote se pehle `f` hota hai. `{}` ke andar jo bhi ho, uski jagah uski value aa jaati hai.

cards.title: Numbers without the fuss
cards.body: Joining text and a number with `+` is an error. An f-string converts the number for you, and `{}` can hold a calculation.

hi.title: Numbers bina jhanjhat ke
hi.body: Text aur number ko `+` se jodna error hai. f-string number ko aapke liye convert kar deta hai, aur `{}` mein calculation bhi aa sakti hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: Python stops with a `TypeError` here. Tap the line that causes it.
cards.code:
city = "Pune"
parks = 7
print(city + " has " + parks + " parks.")

bug.fix: Joining text and a number with `+` is an error. An f-string converts the number for you: `print(f"{city} has {parks} parks.")`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Yahan Python `TypeError` dekar ruk jaata hai. Us line par tap karo jo iski wajah hai.
hi.fix: Text aur number ko `+` se jodna error hai. f-string number ko aapke liye convert kar deta hai: `print(f"{city} has {parks} parks.")`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: The braces hold a calculation, and the f-string puts its result, 10, in their place.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Braces mein ek calculation hai, aur f-string uski jagah uska result, 10, daal deta hai.

exercise.prompt: Read a name and then an age, each on its own line, and print `<name> is <age> years old.` using an f-string. For `Ada` and `36`, print `Ada is 36 years old.`
exercise.promptHi: Ek naam aur phir ek age padho, dono alag lines mein, aur f-string se `<name> is <age> years old.` print karo. `Ada` aur `36` ke liye `Ada is 36 years old.` print karo.
